subject: Your Apple ID has been locked

message.subject: Your Apple ID has been locked
message.excerpt: Your Apple ID was locked for security reasons. Verify your account to unlock it: https://xn--pple-43d.example/unlock

findings.title: Domain mixes alphabets
evidence: xn--pple-43d[.]example mixes letters from different alphabets
findings.lesson: Some letters in other alphabets are identical to English ones. That 'a' might not be an 'a'.

findings.title: A link points at a lookalike domain
evidence: Link to xn--pple-43d[.]example reads like apple[.]com once lookalike characters are folded (imitating Apple)
findings.lesson: Hover before you click. The link's domain, not its text, tells you where you'll land.

findings.title: Sender domain imitates a known domain
evidence: Sender domain xn--pple-43d[.]example reads like apple[.]com once lookalike characters are folded (imitating Apple)
findings.lesson: Read the domain letter by letter. Attackers register names that look right at a glance.

findings.title: Display name poses as a brand
evidence: Display name "Apple ID" claims Apple, sent from xn--pple-43d[.]example
findings.lesson: The name on a message is free text. Check the address, not just who it says it is.

findings.title: Talks as a brand, links nowhere near it
evidence: Opens as Apple but neither the sender nor any link uses a domain that belongs to it
findings.lesson: When a message says it's from a well-known company, go to that company's site yourself instead of using the link.

findings.title: Internationalised domain name
findings.lesson: Domains starting with 'xn--' hide non-English letters. Be wary when one shows up in a message about your account.
